reading.title: Different People, One Team
reading.passage: When Aisha joined a new school in Sohar, she worried that her classmates would not understand her interests. She loved astronomy and usually spent Friday evenings looking at the night sky. Her desk partner, Salma, enjoyed art and was always drawing. At first, the girls had little to talk about. Then their teacher asked the class to organise a display about personal identity. Aisha suggested a simple model of the solar system while Salma offered to design the posters. They invited two other pupils: Hamad, who was confident speaking to visitors, and Noura, who preferred organising details quietly. The project succeeded because each student contributed a different strength. Aisha now believes identity is not only about appearance or nationality; it also includes values, habits, abilities and the way people treat one another. She still enjoys astronomy, but she is learning that sharing an interest can be easier when she listens to other people first.

questions.stem: Why was Aisha worried at first?
options: She thought others would not understand her interests

questions.stem: What did Salma contribute to the display?
Which pupil was confident speaking to visitors?
What did Aisha learn about identity?
options: Different strengths and values are part of it
Everyone must have the same interests

grammar.stem: My sister usually ____ to school by bus.
grammar.explanation: A habit: present simple with she = goes.

grammar.stem: Listen! The pupils ____ a presentation about their hobbies.
grammar.explanation: An action happening now: are giving.

grammar.stem: Faris ____ football on Saturdays; he prefers reading.
grammar.explanation: Frequency adverb with present simple: never plays.

grammar.stem: I ____ this photograph of my grandparents.
grammar.explanation: Love is a stative verb here, so use present simple.

grammar.stem: What ____ your best friend usually do after school?
grammar.explanation: Present simple question with he/she: does.

grammar.stem: At the moment, Noura ____ a personal profile.
grammar.explanation: At the moment signals present continuous.

grammar.stem: She is a very ____ student who always helps new classmates.
grammar.explanation: An adjective describes a student: helpful.

A student who speaks easily to strangers is ____.
A person who tells the truth is ____.
Someone who thinks about other people's feelings is ____.
The phrase 'a personal profile' refers to ____.

writing.title: Personal profile email
writing.prompt: Write an email to a new exchange student. Introduce yourself, describe your personality, explain what you usually do in your free time and mention one activity you are enjoying this month. Use present simple and present continuous appropriately.

writing.title: Identity information sheet
writing.prompt: Write an information sheet about a classmate's interests, strengths and usual habits. Explain why different personalities can help people work together.

reading.title: The Message That Changed a Project
reading.passage: Last term, Mariam and her classmates were making a short film about communication in their town. They interviewed grandparents who remembered sharing news by letter, and younger people who used messaging apps every day. While they were editing the film, a recorded interview disappeared from the shared folder. Everyone thought the file had been deleted. Mariam was checking the computer when she noticed a message from Bilal. He explained that he had moved the recording to a different folder to protect it from accidental changes. Unfortunately, he had forgotten to tell the team. The students felt relieved, but they also realised that a useful action can cause confusion if nobody explains it. They agreed to keep a simple record whenever a file was moved and to listen carefully when someone raised a concern. The finished film showed more than changes in technology: it showed why clear messages, careful listening and trust matter in every generation.

questions.stem: When did the recording seem to disappear?
Why had Bilal moved the file?
options: To send it to a newspaper

questions.stem: What rule did the pupils introduce?
options: Record when a file is moved

grammar.stem: While I ____ to my cousin, the phone suddenly stopped working.
grammar.explanation: A background action interrupted by a shorter past action: was talking.

grammar.stem: The interviewer ____ three questions yesterday.
grammar.explanation: Finished past event: asked.

grammar.stem: We enjoy ____ to stories about our grandparents.
grammar.explanation: Enjoy takes the -ing form.

grammar.stem: She ____ me when I was explaining the problem.
grammar.explanation: A short past action interrupting a longer one: called.

grammar.stem: The students ____ their project when the teacher arrived.
grammar.explanation: Past continuous for action in progress at that past moment.

grammar.stem: I prefer ____ messages to making phone calls.
grammar.explanation: Prefer + -ing is natural in this comparison.

grammar.stem: He ____ the instructions carefully before using the app.
grammar.explanation: Past form of read is spelled 'read'.

vocabulary.stem: She explained the plan ____ the new students.
We talked ____ our project for twenty minutes.
To say a word correctly is to ____ it.
If you understand a message, you know what it ____.

writing.title: Story: a communication mistake
writing.prompt: Write a story about a message that caused a misunderstanding while students were preparing an event. Use past simple and past continuous, describe the problem and show how clear communication solved it.

writing.title: Communication choices
writing.prompt: Explain how people communicate with family and friends today and how this differs from the past. Use at least three expressions connected with speaking, listening or explaining.

reading.title: A Smart Garden with a Human Decision
reading.passage: A group of students at a school in Nizwa is planning a small smart garden. The project will use sensors to measure moisture in the soil, and a simple app will display the results. The students are going to test the first prototype next month. Their science teacher reminds them that a sensor cannot make every decision. For example, the app may report dry soil, but the team must check whether a plant actually needs water before opening the irrigation system. Some pupils think artificial intelligence will make gardening easier; others worry that relying completely on technology could waste water when a sensor breaks. The group is meeting a local engineer on Tuesday to discuss those risks. A school exhibition opens at nine o'clock on Thursday, and the pupils hope to demonstrate the garden there. They will collect feedback and improve the design before producing a larger version. They want to show that useful inventions combine technology with responsible human judgement.

questions.stem: When are students planning to test the prototype?
Why must people check a sensor reading?
What is the main message of the text?
options: Combine technology with responsible human decisions

grammar.stem: I think more schools ____ use solar energy in the future.
grammar.explanation: Prediction: will + base form.

grammar.stem: Look at those dark clouds. It ____ rain.
grammar.explanation: Present evidence supports is going to.

grammar.stem: We ____ the engineer on Tuesday; the appointment is confirmed.
grammar.explanation: Present continuous can express a fixed future arrangement.

grammar.stem: The exhibition ____ at nine o'clock tomorrow.
grammar.explanation: Present simple commonly states timetables.

grammar.stem: Our class ____ build a robot next term; we have already made the plan.
grammar.explanation: Be going to expresses a decided plan.

grammar.stem: If the device fails, we ____ the battery first.
grammar.explanation: First conditional: if + present, will + infinitive.

grammar.stem: Why don't we ____ a clearer instruction poster?
grammar.explanation: Why don't we + base verb introduces a suggestion.

writing.title: Email proposing an invention
writing.prompt: Write an email to your science teacher proposing a useful invention for your school. Explain what it will do, how your team is going to build it, when you are meeting and what problems you may need to solve.

writing.title: Future technology: balanced opinion
writing.prompt: Some people believe AI will improve everyday life, while others worry about relying on it too much. Write a balanced paragraph, give examples and suggest one sensible rule for responsible use.
